descripcion: Agile teams are getting better in executing the development process, but short timelines force some to abandon user research and degrade the resulting user experience.

titulo: Treemaps: Data Visualization of Complex Hierarchies
descripcion: Creating usable, readable treemaps is difficult. They are a complex, area-based data visualization for hierarchical data that can be hard to interpret precisely.

titulo: Tool Abundance in the Digital Workplace: Trendy or Troublesome?
descripcion: With an abundance of digital workplace tools available today, organizations must carefully approach tool curation to preserve employee productivity and their workplace experience.

titulo: Signal–to–Noise Ratio
descripcion: Relevant information is “signal,” while irrelevant information is “noise”. A high signal–to–noise ratio is a key outcome for any UX professional’s work, in terms of both content and page design.

titulo: Usability Testing with Minors: 16 Tips
descripcion: To guarantee an effective study with users under 18-years old, recruit extra participants, design a child-friendly lab, prepare a plethora of age-appropriate tasks, and avoid being too authoritative.

titulo: The Vortex: Why Users Feel Trapped in Their Devices
descripcion: Many users report anxiety and lack of control over the amount of time they spend online. We call this feeling “the Vortex.”

titulo: Field Studies Should Inform Intranet Redesign
etiquetas: field studies and ethnographic methods,Intranets,Research Methods,journey mapping,mental models
descripcion: Observing users in their natural work context unveils mismatches between users’ and designers’ mental models and builds empathy with end users.

titulo: Avoid Leading Questions to Get Better Insights from Participants
etiquetas: User Testing,Research Methods,usability research,facilitating research,field studies and ethnographic methods,Refresher for UX Pros
descripcion: In user research, the facilitator's choice of words can affect the participants' feedback or behavior.

titulo: Remote Usability Tests: Moderated and Unmoderated
descripcion: Remote usability testing allows you to get customer insights when travel budgets are small, timeframes are tight, or test participants are hard to find.

titulo: Long vs. Short Articles as Content Strategy
descripcion: Information foraging shows how to calculate your content strategy's costs and benefits. A mixed diet that combines brief overviews and comprehensive coverage is often best.

titulo: Write Articles, Not Blog Postings
etiquetas: Content Strategy,Social Media,Writing for the Web
descripcion: To demonstrate world-class expertise, avoid quickly written, shallow postings. Instead, invest your time in thorough, value-added content that attracts paying customers.

titulo: Offshore Usability

titulo: International Usability Engineering: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: International usability testing addresses methods and logistical concerns to consider when evaluating the usability of products intended for an international audience.

titulo: Change Blindness in UX: Definition
descripcion: Significant changes in a web page can remain unnoticed when they lack strong cues, due to the limitations of human attention.

titulo: Preventing User Errors: Avoiding Conscious Mistakes
descripcion: Thoughtful design is transparent and easy to understand, provides a preview, and helps users to easily correct their errors.

titulo: Auto-Forwarding Carousels, Accordions Annoy Users & Reduce Visibility
descripcion: The user's target was at the top of the page in 98-point font. But she failed to find it because the panel auto-rotated instead of staying still.

titulo: Show Numbers as Numerals When Writing for Online Readers
descripcion: It's better to use '23' than 'twenty-three' to catch users' eyes when they scan Web pages for facts, according to eyetracking data.

titulo: What B2B Designers Can Learn from B2C About Building Trust
etiquetas: B2B Websites,trust and credibility,Ecommerce,Psychology and UX,behavioral economics,emotional design
descripcion: Even though B2B and B2C ecommerce sites have different kinds of users, both types of sites can use similar strategies to simplify purchase flows and increase consumer trust.

titulo: 'About Us' Information on Corporate Websites - User Research Findings
etiquetas: Corporate Websites,B2B Websites,Writing for the Web,trust and credibility
descripcion: Users expect About Us sections to be clear, authentic, and transparent. They compare corporate content with third-party reviews to form a holistic opinion of a company before initiating business or applying for jobs.

titulo: How to Display Taxes, Fees, and Shipping Charges on Ecommerce Sites
descripcion: Unexpected service fees and special-delivery costs should be disclosed early in the shopping process to avoid losing customers.

titulo: Intelligent Assistants: Users’ Attitudes Toward Alexa, Google Assistant, and Siri
etiquetas: voice interfaces,Artificial Intelligence,internet of things,Psychology and UX,mental models,emotional design,Interaction Design,new technologies,trust and credibility
descripcion: Users assume that assistants have a low level of competence for complex tasks and find them to be socially awkward to interact with.

titulo: Plain Language Is for Everyone, Even Experts
etiquetas: expertise,Writing for the Web,trust and credibility
descripcion: Professionals want clear, concise information devoid of unnecessary jargon or complex terms. Plain language is a necessity and benefits both consumers and organizations.

titulo: Hierarchy of Trust: The 5 Experiential Levels of Website Commitment
descripcion: Sites must meet users' basic trust needs before asking for visitor information. The trust pyramid has 5 levels of user commitment, with separate design rules.

titulo: Social Proof in the User Experience
descripcion: People are guided by other people’s behavior, so we can represent the actions, beliefs, and advice of the crowd in a design to influence users.

titulo: Trust or Bust: Communicating Trustworthiness in Web Design
descripcion: The Web is turning into a low-trust society, hurting the honest sites. Site design can communicate trustworthiness in several ways, though ultimately the customer's actual experience is what matters.

titulo: The Anchoring Principle
etiquetas: Persuasive Design,behavioral economics,Psychology and UX,learning,recommendations,mental models
descripcion: People tend to focus on a single, initial piece of information, which influences how they estimate value and make subsequent decisions.

titulo: What Is Design Thinking, Really? (What Practitioners Say)
descripcion: The majority of UX and design professionals define design thinking roughly the same, regardless of industry and experience, but there’s no agreement on the specifics.

titulo: Define Stronger A/B Test Variations Through UX Research
descripcion: Complement A/B split tests with user research to identify true causes and develop well informed design variations.

titulo: Putting A/B Testing in Its Place
descripcion: Measuring the live impact of design changes on key business metrics is valuable, but often creates a focus on short-term improvements. This near-term view neglects bigger issues that only qualitative studies can find.

titulo: Large Devices Preferred for Important Tasks
descripcion: Despite substantial improvements in mobile UX over the past decade, people still tend to do their most important online activities on larger screens.

titulo: Setup of an Eyetracking Study
descripcion: If you’re planning on running your own eyetracking study, pay attention to equipment, supplies, and placement to ensure high quality data.

titulo: The Attention Economy
descripcion: Digital products are competing for users’ limited attention. The modern economy increasingly revolves around the human attention span and how products capture that attention.

titulo: 6 Rules for Persuasive Storytelling
etiquetas: storytelling,Persuasive Design,Design Process,emotional design,stakeholders,deliverables,Customer Journeys,journey mapping,Personas
descripcion: Stories build empathy and make the user needs and pain points memorable to your team. Effective stories speak the language of the audience, are rooted in data, and take advantage of compelling artifacts.

titulo: In-Store & Online: Designing For the Changing Behaviors of Today’s Shoppers
descripcion: Different shopping channels come with relative pros and cons; understand them, augment the channel capabilities whenever possible, and support expected customers’ crosschannel transitions.

titulo: Beyond Usability: 3 User Experiences Reshaping Their Industries
etiquetas: service design,Customer Journeys,Branding,emotional design,Application Design,case studies
descripcion: Rent the Runway, Uber, and Airbnb challenge the traditional experiences of their industries through deep design, not just screen-UI design.

titulo: Priming and User Interfaces
descripcion: Exposure to a stimulus influences behavior in subsequent, possibly unrelated tasks. This is called priming; priming effects abound in usability and web design.

titulo: Scrolling and Attention
descripcion: People scroll vertically more than they used to, but new eyetracking data shows that they will still look more above the page fold than below it.

titulo: Alternative Payment Methods Enable International Purchases
descripcion: By understanding customers’ payment preferences and offering options that people are used to in their own country, sites can improve the checkout experience for international purchasers.

titulo: Applying Discounts and Promotions on Ecommerce Websites
descripcion: Coupons and other discounts should be easy to apply and shopping carts should clearly display how the total was affected by the promotion.

titulo: The Mobile Checkout Experience
descripcion: Optimize the checkout experience on mobile ecommerce channels by taking into account the strengths and limitations of mobile devices. Minimize typing and use capabilities like geolocation and the camera.

titulo: The New Ecommerce User Experience: Changes in Users’ Expectations
descripcion: Powerhouse retail platforms shape customers’ expectations for a stellar online-shopping experience.

titulo: Store Finders: Why People Still Need Locator Links
descripcion: Providing contextual access to a locator tool in key areas throughout a site makes it easy for users to find a store within the context of a broader task.

titulo: 4 Noteworthy Intranet Design Trends in 2019
etiquetas: Intranets,intranet design annual,intranet design annual winners
descripcion: Striking trends from this years’ Intranet Design Annual include user-targeted search, core task support, launch fanfare, and integrated access to key tools.

titulo: Young Adults Appreciate Flat Design More than Their Parents Do
descripcion: 18-to-25-year olds gave slightly higher ratings of flat designs than older adults. That increased aesthetic appeal may not be worth the cost of flat design.

titulo: The Characteristics of Minimalism in Web Design
descripcion: The 5 defining features of minimalist interfaces are: flat design, limited color schemes, few UI elements, use of negative space, and dramatic typography.

titulo: Test Paper Prototypes to Save Time and Money: The Mozilla Case Study
descripcion: Low-fidelity user testing of several iterations of Mozilla’s Support website quickly showed which user-interface elements worked best for Firefox users.

titulo: Mobile Websites: Mobile-Dedicated, Responsive, Adaptive, or Desktop Site?
descripcion: Different approaches to implementing mobile websites have each their advantages and disadvantages. All should follow the same mobile user-experience principles.

titulo: Maps and Location Finders on Mobile Devices
etiquetas: locator tools,Ecommerce,Mobile & Tablet,mobile web,graphical user interfaces,ui elements
descripcion: Maps of business locations may be more visually appealing than a simple list view, but they introduce too many usability issues on mobile devices.

titulo: Tesla’s Touchscreen UI: A Case Study of Car-Dashboard User Interface
descripcion: Vehicle controls should be easily accessible and require minimum attention from drivers, while driving-related information should be displayed clearly and understandably.

titulo: Multivariate vs. A/B Testing: Incremental vs. Radical Changes
descripcion: Multivariate tests indicate how various UI elements interact with each other and are a tool for making incremental improvements to a design.

titulo: Intranet Information Architecture (IA) Trends
descripcion: Intranets are improving findability and discoverability by organizing content by task, using mega-menus, offering wayfinding cues, and providing shortcuts.

titulo: How to Run a Usability Test with Users Who Are on Your Site Right Now
descripcion: Learn how to use tools like ethnio and GoToMeeting to recruit participants while they’re on your site and immediately run moderated usability studies.

titulo: Don’t Use Split Buttons for Navigation Menus
etiquetas: buttons,responsive design,Mobile & Tablet,Navigation,graphical user interfaces,touch targets
descripcion: Menu on hover, category landing page on click: we discuss challenges and solutions for replicating this pattern on touchscreens.

titulo: Which Comes First? Layout or Content?
descripcion: Avoid awkward and difficult page layouts by fitting flexible templates to content whenever possible. Test often during design, and plan to scale up.

titulo: A Few Mobile UX Design Skills Help With Very Large Touchscreen UX Design
descripcion: Users’ field of vision, arm motion, affordance, and privacy are a few of the design considerations for very large touchscreens (kiosks and other nonmobile use).

titulo: iOS Design Rules to Break
descripcion: Reconsider using iOS recommended design patterns: Page control (dots), Submit at top, the Plus (+) and Move icons, because they cause usability problems in testing.

titulo: Mobile User Experience: Limitations and Strengths
descripcion: Mobile design must reflect smartphone constraints and strengths: small screen, short sessions, single window, touch interaction, GPS and other phone features.

titulo: Mobile Navigation: Image Grids or Text Lists?
descripcion: For mobile navigation, image grids should be saved for deeper IA levels where visual differentiation between menu items is critical.

titulo: Windows 8 — Disappointing Usability for Both Novice and Power Users
descripcion: Hidden features, reduced discoverability, cognitive overhead from dual environments, and reduced power from a single-window UI and low information density. Too bad.

titulo: Kindle Fire HD: Much Better Than Original Kindle Fire
descripcion: Amazon's new Kindle Fire has much better usability than last year's model—and the 7-inch tablet beats the 9-inch version.

titulo: iPad Usability: First Findings From User Testing
descripcion: iPad apps are inconsistent and have low feature discoverability, with frequent user errors due to accidental gestures. An overly strong print metaphor and weird interaction styles cause further usability problems.

titulo: Usability Labs Survey: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: This article summarizes statistics for 13 usability laboratories. It also gives an introduction to the main uses of usability laboratories in usability engineering and surveys some of the issues related to practical use of user testing and computer-aided usability engineering.

titulo: Noncommand User Interfaces: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: New user interface technologies beyond the flat screen, and twelve dimensions across which future user interfaces may differ: user focus, the computer's role, interface control, syntax, object visibility, interaction stream, bandwidth, tracking feedback, interface locus, user programming, and software packaging.

titulo: Technology Transfer of Usability Inspection Methods (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Participants in a course on usability inspection methods were surveyed 7-8 months after the course. Factors which influenced adoption were cost, rated benefit of the method, relevance to current projects, and whether the methods had active evangelists.

titulo: Outliers and Luck in User Performance
descripcion: 6% of task attempts are extremely slow and constitute outliers in measured user performance. These sad incidents are caused by bad luck that designers can - and should - eradicate.

titulo: Large Touchscreens: What's Different?
descripcion: Designing for larger-scale touchscreens requires particular attention to input, screen focus, and privacy.

titulo: Children’s Exposure to Digital Technology Causes Parental Anxiety
descripcion: While North American parents are concerned with the impact of technology on their kids’ social and emotional development, Chinese parents worry about health and academic effects.

titulo: Using Swipe to Trigger Contextual Actions
descripcion: Implementations of swipe-to-delete or swipe to reveal contextual actions often suffer from usability problems.

titulo: UX Certification: NN/g Awards First Person
descripcion: Nielsen Norman Group launches UX Certification. Training and exams boost knowledge and authority. Ian Thompson was the first certified.

titulo: "Top Ten Mistakes" Revisited Three Years Later
descripcion: 9 of 10 mistakes in Web design identified in May 1996 continued to cause severe usability problems years later and should be avoided in modern websites.

titulo: Who Commits The "Top Ten Mistakes" of Web Design?
descripcion: Major websites violate on average 16% of the top ten mistakes in Web design; huge corporate sites have many more design mistakes than the most popular sites.

titulo: Email Newsletters: Surviving Inbox Congestion
descripcion: Newsletter usability has increased since our last study, but the competition for users' attention has also grown with the ever-increasing glut of information.

titulo: How to Respond to Skepticism of Testing Small Groups of Users
descripcion: “That’s just one person” and “Our real users aren’t like that” are common objections to findings from qualitative usability testing. Address these concerns proactively to ensure your research is effective.

titulo: Bush vs. Kerry: Email Newsletters Rated
descripcion: Both candidates for president of the United States offer email newsletters with much good content to excite supporters, but miserable subscription interfaces and several other usability problems.

titulo: Mastery, Mystery, and Misery: The Ideologies of Web Design
descripcion: Simple, unobtrusive designs that support users are successful because they abide by the Web's nature -- and they make people feel good.

titulo: 8 Steps to Prepare for the Holiday Shopping Season
descripcion: Reduce the bounce rate for organic landing pages, collect data to manage PPC for maximum ROI, and take 6 other steps to maximize your site's holiday sales potential before it's too late.

titulo: Informational Articles Must Ask For the Order
descripcion: Unless you have explicit links to product pages from article content, users who visit articles directly from search engines might never realize that you sell related products.

titulo: After the Buy Button in E-Commerce
descripcion: The best way for e-commerce sites to increase subsequent orders is to treat customers well after they place their initial order.

titulo: Remote Control Anarchy
descripcion: The 6 remote controls required for a simple home theater illustrate the problems caused by complexity and inconsistency in user interfaces.

titulo: Ten Best Government Intranets
descripcion: Redesigning an intranet for usability often more than doubled the use of these award-winning designs from ten public-sector organizations.

titulo: B2B: Help Your Fans Convince Their Bosses
descripcion: B2B websites must support a more complex buying process than B2C sites. Three key goals are to make a buyer's shortlist, offer a downloadable advocacy kit, and build a reputation for great service.

titulo: Why Mobile Phones are Annoying
descripcion: Bystanders rated mobile-phone conversations as dramatically more noticeable, intrusive, and annoying than conversations conducted face-to-face. While volume was an issue, hearing only half a discussion also seemed to up the irritation factor.

titulo: Statistics for Traffic Referred by Search Engines and Navigation Directories to Useit
descripcion: Server logs from www.useit.ocm shows sharply increasing traffic from Google in 2001. Referrer statistics may be a leading indicator for portal success.

titulo: Why Consumer Products Have Inferior User Experience
descripcion: Physical products, from consumer electronics to cars, are needlessly complex because they're developed by insular companies that continue to ignore the growing usability trend.

titulo: Targeted Email Newsletters Show Continued Strength
descripcion: E-newsletters that are informative, convenient, and timely are often preferred over other media. However, a new study found that only 11% of newsletters were read thoroughly, so layout and content scannability are paramount.

titulo: How Big is the Difference Between Websites?
descripcion: The average difference in measured usability between competing websites is 68%. This is smaller than expected, but makes sense given the dynamics of design within individual industries.

titulo: Productivity in the Service Economy
descripcion: Yes, it is possible for white-collar workers to work smarter and become more productive. While intranet usability provides substantial initial gains, workflow usability can go much further and will save millions of jobs.

titulo: Ten Steps for Cleaning Up Information Pollution
descripcion: Better prioritization, fewer interruptions, and concentrated information that's easy to find and manage helps people become more productive and stop wasting their colleagues' time.

titulo: Top 10 Web Design Mistakes of 2003
descripcion: Sites are getting better at using minimalist design, maintaining archives, and offering comprehensive services. However, these advances entail their own usability problems, as several prominent mistakes from 2003 show.

titulo: Two Sigma: Usability and Six Sigma Quality Assurance
descripcion: On average across many test tasks, users fail 35% of the time when using websites. This is 100,000 times worse than six sigma's requirement, but Web usability can still benefit from a six sigma quality approach.

titulo: Alertbox #200
descripcion: I've published 200 Alertbox columns on the Web since 1995; in addition to achieving key victories over multi-million-dollar special interests and enemies of usability, the column's readership statistics validate the practice of archiving content.

titulo: Misconceptions About Usability
descripcion: Misconceptions about usability's expense, the time it involves, and its creative impact prevent companies from getting crucial user data, as does the erroneous belief that existing customer-feedback methods are a valid driver for interface design.

titulo: Mobile Devices: One Generation From Useful
descripcion: New mobile devices show a huge improvement over previous generations, but they're still not good enough to score a real win. To get there, we need both PC-integrated applications and specialized mobile services rather than repurposed website content.

titulo: Gateway Pages Prevent PDF Shock
descripcion: Spare your users the misery of being dumped into PDF files without warning. Create special gateway pages that summarize the contents of big documents and guide users gently into the PDF morass.

titulo: Diversity Is Power for Specialized Sites
descripcion: Small websites get less traffic than big ones, but they can still dominate their niches. For each question users ask, the Web delivers a different set of sites to provide the answers.

titulo: Usability for $200
descripcion: How can a small company's website benefit from usability activities despite a minuscule budget? By integrating four simple and effective usability practices into the design process.

titulo: Making Web Advertisements Work
descripcion: Web users are highly goal-driven, and ads that interfere with their goals will be ignored. To succeed, ads must work with the medium, as well as with the user's aims and mindset.

titulo: Will Plain-Text Ads Continue to Rule?
descripcion: Text-only advertisements work far better than banners, but is this only due to their novelty? Search engine text ads will retain their superiority over time, but text ads on other sites will work only if they focus on directly meeting users' needs.

titulo: Convincing Clients to Pay for Usability
descripcion: Professionally run design agencies user test their designs to increase the value they deliver to their clients. The challenge is getting clients to understand the benefits of a solid development methodology.

titulo: Intranet Portals: A Tool Metaphor for Corporate Information
descripcion: Internet portals are virtually dead, but a portal approach can tame the unruly chaos on internal company networks. Intranet portals overcome many Internet portal limitations, and might be the best hope for productivity and a unified user experience.

titulo: Low-End Media for User Empowerment
descripcion: Fancy media on websites typically fails user testing. Simple text and clear photos not only communicate better with users, they also enhance users' feeling of control and thus support the Web's mission as an instant gratification environment.

titulo: Do Productivity Increases Generate Economic Gains?
descripcion: Usability improvements can save time-on-task, but critics argue that this is not the same as saving money. Others worry that productivity gains cause unemployment. Neither is correct: usable design saves money and saves jobs.

titulo: PR on Websites: Increasing Usability
descripcion: Compared with a similar 2001 study, a new study of journalists as they looked for information on corporate websites' PR areas showed significant usability improvements: a 5% higher success rate and 15% increased guidelines compliance.

titulo: Voice Interfaces: Assessing the Potential
descripcion: Visual interfaces are inherently superior to auditory interfaces for many tasks. The Star Trek fantasy of speaking to your computer is not the most fruitful path to usable systems.

titulo: Employee Directory Search: Resolving Conflicting Usability Guidelines
descripcion: Guidelines conflict on whether to limit intranet search to a single search box or dedicate an additional box to employee directory searches. There's theory to support both guidelines. What's up?

titulo: Persuasive Design: New Captology Book
descripcion: Review of B.J. Fogg's new Persuasive Technology book, which provides useful principles on how to think about creating persuasive design, but rarely gives detailed design guidelines. The exception is a section on enhancing website credibility.

titulo: Top 10 Web Design Mistakes of 2002
descripcion: Every year brings new mistakes. In 2002, several of the worst mistakes in Web design related to poor email integration. The number one mistake, however, was lack of pricing information, followed by overly literal search engines.

titulo: In the Future, We'll All Be Harry Potter
descripcion: The world of magic is a world where inanimate objects come alive; it's as if they had computational power, sensors, awareness, and connectivity.

titulo: Ephemeral Web-Based Applications
descripcion: Usability tests of 46 Flash applications identified basic issues related to the ephemeral nature of Web-embedded apps. Some findings restate old truths about GUIs; others reflect the Net's new status as nexus of the user experience.

titulo: Intranet Usability: The Trillion-Dollar Question
descripcion: The average mid-sized company could gain $5 million per year in employee productivity by improving its intranet design to the top quartile level of a cross-company intranet usability study. The return on investment? One thousand percent or more.

titulo: Making Flash Usable for Users With Disabilities
descripcion: Flash designs are easier for users with disabilities to use when designers combine visual and textual presentations, minimize incessant movement, decrease spacing between related objects, and simplify features.

titulo: Celebrating Holidays and Special Occasions on Websites
descripcion: Even small holiday decorations can increase joy of use and make websites feel more current and more connected to users' lives and physical environment. The key is to commemorate without detracting from your users' main reasons for visiting the site.

titulo: Email Newsletters Pick Up Where Websites Leave Off
descripcion: Users have highly emotional reactions to newsletters which feel much more personal than websites. In usability testing, success rates were high for subscribe and unsubscribe tasks, but users were frustrated by newsletters that demanded too much of their time.

titulo: Making the Physical Environment Interactive
descripcion: Tiny motors and sensors will make physical objects interactive and create a renaissance for gestural user interfaces. As interface design moves from the screen to the material world, the need for simple, easy to use designs will only increase.

titulo: Becoming a Usability Professional
descripcion: A successful usability career requires some theoretical knowledge, but mainly rests on brainpower and many years' experience testing and studying users. The only way to gain that experience is to start now.

titulo: User Empowerment and the Fun Factor
descripcion: Designs that engage and empower users increase their enjoyment and encourage them to explore websites in-depth. Once we achieve ease of use, we'll need additional usability methods to further strengthen joy of use.

titulo: Reduce Redundancy: Decrease Duplicated Design Decisions
descripcion: UX complexity increases when a single feature or hypertext link is repeated on a page. Users rarely recognize duplicates as such, wasting time repeating efforts.

titulo: Improving Usability Guideline Compliance
descripcion: Over the last 1.5 years, the average compliance with established usability guidelines increased by 4%. If we can sustain this level of improvement, we'll reach the ideal of 90% guideline compliance in 2017.

titulo: Foreword to Rosenfeld and Morville's Information Architecture (2nd ed)
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's foreword to Rosenfeld and Morville's book on Web Information Architecture (second edition). Your users will get lost unless you follow their advice.

titulo: Supporting Multiple-Location Users
descripcion: About half of the users now access the Internet from more than one location. Despite the implications of this for service design, many systems assume that users remain bound to a single computer.

titulo: Top Research Laboratories in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)
descripcion: A core group of elite corporate research labs (and a few universities) defined the field of human-computer interaction and established much of whatever ease of use we now enjoy. With big labs disappearing, the future of HCI research is in jeopardy.

titulo: Protecting the User's Mailbox
descripcion: Email is a powerful way to reach customers, but overdoing it is risky. Let users know up front that you'll respect their mailboxes. Otherwise, they won't give their email addresses, and you'll lose a unique channel for marketing and customer service.

titulo: Deep Linking is Good Linking
descripcion: Links that go directly to a site's interior pages enhance usability because, unlike generic links, they specifically relate to users' goals. Websites should encourage deep linking and follow three guidelines to support its users.

titulo: Official Winter Olympics Site: Not Even Bronze
descripcion: An early tweaking raised the Salt Lake City website to 70% compliance with homepage usability guidelines. Inside the site, however, task support falls far below medal contention.

titulo: Site Map Usability, 1st study
descripcion: Most site maps fail to convey multiple levels of the site's information architecture. In usability tests, users often overlook site maps or can't find them. Complexity is also a problem: a map should be a map, not a navigational challenge of its own.

titulo: Avoiding Commodity Status
descripcion: PCs do not need to be commodities: a focus on quality can differentiate both products and services. Software has great potential for getting better, as shown by an under-appreciated feature in Windows XP that can save users $2,000 per year.

titulo: Consistency in User Interface Design, Preface 2002 Reprint Edition
descripcion: Preface to the 2002 reprint of Jakob Nielsen's classic book from 1989 about user interface consistency.

titulo: Salary Survey: User Experience Professionals 2001
descripcion: Salary data from 1,078 user experience professionals in United States, Europe, Asia, and Australia. A usability specialist in California with five years' experience averaged $90,118 in 2001.

titulo: User Payments: Predictions for 2001 Revisited
descripcion: Advertising-supported websites will soon be a thing of the past. As I predicted a year ago, sites began charging for services in 2001. Although most sites are still not handling payments right, two innovative European projects hold much hope for 2002.

titulo: DVD Menu Design: The Failures of Web Design Recreated Yet Again
descripcion: Designers of DVDs have failed to profit from the lessons of previous media. DVD menu structures are baroque, less usable, less pleasurable, less effective. It is time to take DVD design as seriously as we do web design. The field needs discipline, attention, to the User Experience, and standardization of control and display formats.

titulo: Deferred Hypertext: The Virtues of Delayed Gratification
descripcion: Navigating a full browsing session to find information can be unpleasant and slow, particularly on mobile devices. Instead, issue a deferred request and have the information arrive later, as done by some SMS systems.

titulo: The End of Homemade Websites
descripcion: Web services will free individual site designers from having to program and design common features. This will decrease business costs, increase usability, and let designers focus on and improve features that are unique to each site.

titulo: Top 10 Application-Design Mistakes
descripcion: Application usability is enhanced when the UI guides and supports users through the workflow.

titulo: Top 10 Application-Design Mistakes of 2008
descripcion: Application usability is enhanced when users know how to operate the UI and it guides them through the workflow. Violating common guidelines prevents both.

titulo: Risks of Quantitative Studies
descripcion: Number fetishism leads usability studies astray by focusing on statistical analyses that are often false, biased, misleading, or overly narrow. Better to emphasize insights and qualitative research.

titulo: Interface Copy Impacts Decision Making
descripcion: The language used in interfaces influences the decisions that our users will make. Manipulative copy nudges users towards making choices that are against their best interests.

titulo: Usability Problems Found by Heuristic Evaluation (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Heuristic evaluation is a good method of identifying both major and minor problems with an interface, but the lists of usability problems found by heuristic evaluation will tend to be dominated by minor problems, which is one reason severity ratings form a useful supplement to the method.

titulo: Usability Inspection Method Summary: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Usability inspection is a group of methods where experts inspect a user interface to discover usability problems, the severity of the usability problems, and the overall usability of an entire system.

etiquetas: Agile,UX Teams,Site Optimization,Collaboration & Teams,UX Leadership & Management,definition,Design Process
descripcion: Like technical debt, user-experience debt piles up over time and, if left unaddressed, will lead to compounding user problems and costly, time-consuming cleanup efforts. Agile solutions for prioritizing and resolving UX-debt issues can be adapted to other environments.

titulo: The Dangers of Overpersonalization
descripcion: Too much personalization leads to homogeneous experiences for users and can generate content fatigue and lack of diversity.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
etiquetas: International Users,new technologies,Mobile & Tablet,Web Usability,Social Media,integration,conversational interfaces,china
descripcion: User research finds that tightly integrated services with simple and unified design make people use WeChat; mainly through traditional GUI interactions.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
descripcion: Hero images, carousels, fat footers, video, minimalist design, and responsive navigation, are among some of the top feature trends of the best intranets of 2016.

titulo: Branding an Intranet
descripcion: The name of the intranet, its logo, and the visual relationship with the company’s external website are key elements to consider when establishing a brand and an identity for your intranet.

titulo: Breadcrumb Navigation Increasingly Useful
descripcion: One line of text shows a page's location in the site hierarchy. User testing shows many benefits and no downsides to breadcrumbs for secondary navigation.

titulo: Designing for Kids: Cognitive Considerations
descripcion: Designers should use clear and specific instructions and leverage mental models to facilitate smooth and successful user experiences for children.

titulo: Kinect Gestural UI: First Impressions
descripcion: Inconsistent gestures, invisible commands, overlooked warnings, awkward dialog confirmations. But fun to play.

titulo: Incompetent Research Skills Curb Users' Problem Solving
descripcion: Users increasingly rely on individual pages listed by search engines instead of finding better ways to tackle problems.

titulo: Animation for Attention and Comprehension
etiquetas: animation,Design Patterns,Human Computer Interaction,Visual Design,ui elements
descripcion: Motion is a powerful tool to attract users’ attention. When designing an animation consider its goal, its frequency of occurrence, and its mechanics.

titulo: UX Guidelines for Recommended Content
descripcion: Encourage engagement with recommendations by presenting them prominently, segmenting suggestions into clear categories, and providing methods for users to give feedback.

titulo: Individualized Recommendations: Users’ Expectations & Assumptions
descripcion: Users appreciate personalized content suggestions and are willing to give up some of their privacy for quality recommendations, while accepting some inaccurate recommendations.

titulo: Salary Trends for UX Professionals (1998-2019)
descripcion: Over the last several years, entry-level UX salaries have dropped, while pay for experienced user experience staff has been more stable. (Updated to 2019.)

titulo: Archiving Usability Reports
descripcion: Most usability practitioners don't derive full value from their user tests because they don't systematically archive the reports. An intranet-based usability archive offers four substantial benefits.

titulo: International Sites: Minimum Requirements
descripcion: Users from other countries have special needs related to entry fields for names and addresses, measurements and dates, and information about regional product standards.

titulo: Alertbox: 10 Years
descripcion: 300,000 words of usability essays have had an impact: online user interfaces are considerably easier to use now than they were in 1995. Many predictions and recommendations have come true, though the full Alertbox vision is far from realized.

titulo: The Canonical Intranet Homepage
descripcion: Intranet homepages have become very similar in their basic layout. Intranets that look the same can nonetheless differ drastically in usability due to different features and content.

titulo: Mental Models For Search Are Getting Firmer
descripcion: Users now have precise expectations for the behavior of search. Designs that invoke this mental model but work differently are confusing.

titulo: Formal Usability Reports vs. Quick Findings
descripcion: Formal reports are the most common way of documenting usability studies, but informal reports are faster to produce and are often a better choice.

titulo: Evangelizing Usability: Change Your Strategy at the Halfway Point
descripcion: The evangelism strategies that help a usability group get established in a company are different from the ones needed to create a full-fledged usability culture.

titulo: Authentic Behavior in User Testing
descripcion: Despite being an artificial situation, user testing generates realistic findings because people engage strongly with the tasks and suspend their disbelief.

titulo: Reviving Advanced Hypertext
descripcion: To manage a huge, worldwide information space, users need proven features like fat links, typed links, integrated search and browsing, overview maps, big-screen designs, and physical hypertext.

titulo: Situate Follow-Ups in Context
descripcion: Make new or follow-up information easily accessible from the location of the original information or transaction.

titulo: The Most Hated Advertising Techniques (Original Research)
descripcion: Studies of how people react to online advertisements have identified several design techniques that impact the user experience very negatively.

titulo: Undoing the Industrial Revolution
descripcion: The last 200 years have driven centralization and changed the human experience in ways that conflict with evolution. The Internet will reestablish a more balanced, decentralized lifestyle.

titulo: Acting on User Research
descripcion: User research offers a learning opportunity that can help you build an understanding of user behavior, but you must resolve discrepancies between research findings and your own beliefs.

titulo: User Education Is Not the Answer to Security Problems
descripcion: Internet scams cannot be thwarted by placing the burden on users to defend themselves at all times. Beleaguered users need protection, and the technology must change to provide this.

titulo: Newsletter Usability: Can a Professional Publisher Do Better?
descripcion: The Washington Post's email newsletter earns a high usability score. It's particularly good at setting users' expectations before they subscribe, though the unsubscribe interface has some problems.

titulo: Five Mistakes in Designing Mobile Push Notifications
descripcion: Provide value to users before asking them to receive your app’s notifications; tell them what the notifications will be about. Don’t send notifications in bursts; make it easy to turn them off.

titulo: Variable Fonts and Wide-Screen Layouts: Adopting Data-Driven Progressive Enhancements
etiquetas: responsive design,Design Patterns,homepages,new technologies,response time,web trends,Visual Design,Site Optimization,screen size
descripcion: The NN/g website homepage now incorporates variable fonts and a wide-screen layout — 2 technical adjustments which improve the user experience for a subset of users on supported devices.

titulo: Filling the Silence with Digital Noise
descripcion: Many people use digital media to avoid silence or empty time.

titulo: WAP Mobile Phones Field Study Findings
descripcion: Following a UK field study, 70% of users decided not to continue using WAP mobile phones. Mobile's killer app is killing time; m-commerce's prospects are dim for the next several years. Current services are poorly designed, have insufficient task analysis, and abuse existing non-mobile design guidelines.

titulo: Segment Analytics Data Using Personas
descripcion: Persona-inspired segments can be used in website analytics to uncover trends in data and derive UX insights. Better than lumping everybody together or segmenting on demographics that don't relate to user behavior.

titulo: Traveling Usability Lab
descripcion: User testing can be done anywhere; witness our international studies, carried out with equipment that fit in a carry-on bag.

titulo: Information Pollution
descripcion: Excessive word count and worthless details are making it harder for people to extract useful information. The more you say, the more people tune out your message.

titulo: Wishlist or shopping cart? Saving products for later in ecommerce
descripcion: On ecommerce sites, saving shopping-cart items for possible later purchase must be discoverable and low-effort.

titulo: Microinteractions in User Experience
descripcion: Microinteractions convey system status, support error prevention, and communicate brand. They are initiated by a trigger, are single-purpose, and can make the experience engaging.

titulo: Change Blindness Causes People to Ignore What Designers Expect Them to See
descripcion: People often overlook new visual details added to an existing image. This affects the usability of many design elements, from error messages to navigation.

titulo: Collaborative Agile Activities Reduce Silos and Align Perspectives
descripcion: All members of an Agile team, regardless of design skills, can contribute to the design of a product or feature during the development process.

titulo: Show Prices for Common Scenarios
descripcion: B2B sites often have overly complex pricing structures or can't show prices at all. To help prospects with early research, list representative cases and their prices.

titulo: Hyped Web Stories Are Irrelevant
descripcion: The fads and big deals that get the press coverage are not important for running a workhorse website. To serve your customers, it's far better to emphasize simplicity and quality than to chase buzzwords.

titulo: Users Interleave Sites and Genres
descripcion: When working on business problems, users flitter among sites, alternating visits to different service genres. No single website defines the user experience on its own.

titulo: Talking-Head Video Is Boring Online
descripcion: Eyetracking data show that users are easily distracted when watching video on websites, especially when the video shows a talking head and is optimized for broadcast rather than online viewing.

titulo: One Billion Internet Users
descripcion: The Internet is growing at an annualized rate of 18% and now has one billion users. A second billion users will follow in the next ten years, bringing a dramatic change in worldwide usability needs.

titulo: Accessibility Is Not Enough
descripcion: A strict focus on accessibility as a scorecard item doesn't help users with disabilities. To help these users accomplish critical tasks, you must adopt a usability perspective.

titulo: Enterprise Usability
descripcion: Usability goes beyond the level of individual users interacting with screens. It's also a question of how easy or cumbersome it is for the entire organization to use a system.

titulo: Incompetent Email Marketing = Lost Future Opportunities
descripcion: Lack of personalization made an email newsletter completely useless to the recipient, damaging long-term customer relationship efforts.

titulo: Intranet Portals Get Streamlined
descripcion: An analysis of intranet portals found slimmer information architectures and a renewed emphasis on fresh content and useful applications. Past findings, including those on role-based personalization, were confirmed.

titulo: Weblog Usability: The Top Ten Design Mistakes
descripcion: Weblogs are often too internally focused and ignore key usability issues, making it hard for new readers to understand the site and trust the author.

titulo: R.I.P. WYSIWYG
descripcion: Macintosh-style interaction design has reached its limits. A new paradigm, called results-oriented UI, might well be the way to empower users in the future.

titulo: Forms vs. Applications
descripcion: Once an online form goes beyond two screenfulls, it's often a sign that the underlying functionality is better supported by an application, which offers a more interactive user experience.

titulo: Time Budgets for Usability Sessions
descripcion: Up to 40% of precious testing time is wasted while users engage in nonessential activities. Far better to focus on watching users perform tasks with the target interface design.

titulo: The Slow Tail: Time Lag Between Visiting and Buying
descripcion: Users often convert to buyers long after their initial visit to a website. A full 5% of orders occur more than 4 weeks after users click on search engine ads.

titulo: Natural Mappings and Stimulus-Response Compatibility in User Interface Design
descripcion: Designs that quickly convey relationships between the user input and the result often use natural mappings or have a high stimulus–response compatibility.

titulo: Mobile Login Methods Help Chinese Users Avoid Password Roadblocks
descripcion: In China, QR-code scanning and verification codes are popular mobile-login alternatives that circumvent the problem of remembering and typing passwords.

titulo: Counterfeit or Credible? UX Design for Authenticity in China
descripcion: In China, websites must gain users’ trust by displaying the company’s local presence, past client work, and availability to answer questions via online chat.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
descripcion: Testing finds that Chinese and Western users experience the same difficulties with complex sites, but Chinese tend to complain less about them and prefer high information density.

titulo: Scan and Shake: A Lesson in Technology Adoption from China’s WeChat
descripcion: QR-code scanning and shake serve as effective ways of communication between the online and the offline worlds and enjoy wider use in China than in the US.

titulo: 6 Ways Ecommerce Sites Can Compete With Amazon
descripcion: Amazon’s size and inventory breadth introduce weakness. Retails should focus on delivering exceptional customer experiences in ways that Amazon cannot.

titulo: Quantitative UX Research in Practice
descripcion: Across 429 UX professionals, 71% of teams report performing some kind of quant UX research at least sometimes, and almost everyone reported struggling with challenges to get quant research done.

titulo: Productivity and Screen Size
descripcion: A study of the benefits of big monitors fails on two accounts: it didn't test realistic tasks, and it didn't test realistic use. Productivity is a key argument for workplace usability, but you must measure it carefully.

titulo: 6 Ways to Fix a Confused Information Architecture
descripcion: When your website's users consistently go to the wrong sections, you have many options for getting users back on track, from better labels to clearer structure.

titulo: User Testing is Not Entertainment
descripcion: Don't run your studies for the benefit of the people in the observation room. Test to discover the truth about the design, even when user tasks are boring to watch.

titulo: Use Old Words When Writing for Findability
descripcion: Familiar words spring to mind when users create their search queries. If your writing favors made-up terms over legacy words, users won't find your site.

titulo: Data Visualization of Web Stats (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Using a linear diagram to plot data from website traffic logs can lead you to overlook important conclusions. Sometimes advanced visualizations are worth the effort.

titulo: Traffic Log Patterns
descripcion: The relative popularity of a site's pages, the number of visitors referred by other sites, and the traffic from search queries continue to follow a Zipf distribution.

titulo: Password Creation: 3 Ways To Make It Easier
descripcion: Ease password creation by showing users the text they type, the password requirements, and a password-strength meter.

titulo: Security & Human Factors
descripcion: A big lie of computer security is that security improves as password complexity increases. In reality, users simply write down difficult passwords, leaving the system vulnerable. Security is better increased by designing for how people actually behave.

titulo: Enterprise Portals Are Popping
descripcion: A usability analysis of 23 intranet portals finds strong growth, increasing collaboration features, and cross-functional governance.

titulo: Is Navigation Useful?
descripcion: Web users go straight for content and ignore navigation areas. Limited structural navigation and local navigation still help, but general navigation should be avoided and generic links minimized to the truly useful.

titulo: Mobile: Native Apps, Web Apps, and Hybrid Apps
descripcion: Native and hybrid apps are installed in an app store; web apps are mobile-optimized webpages that look like an app. Hybrid apps use app-embedded browsers.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: The First Decade
descripcion: Started by Don Norman and Jakob Nielsen in 1998, the company is now 10 years old and has a long list of accomplishments and a much bigger team.

titulo: Life-Long Computer Skills
descripcion: Schools should teach deep, strategic computer insights that can't be learned from reading a manual.

titulo: Do Government Agencies and Non-Profits Get ROI From Usability?
descripcion: Although the gains don't fall into traditional profit columns, there are clear arguments for improving usability of non-commercial websites and intranets. In one example, a state agency could get an ROI of 22,000% by fixing a basic usability problem.

titulo: Wishlists, Gift Certificates, and Gift Giving in E-Commerce
descripcion: Although gift features leverage the online medium and draw new users to a site, they also introduce many usability pitfalls. Among them are poorly designed email notifications, which many users simply ignore.

descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's short list of recommended books about visual interface design (especially Web graphics).

descripcion: Selective list of recommended books on Web design, user interface design, usability engineering, hypertext, future user interfaces (by Jakob Nielsen)

descripcion: User interfaces in film are more exciting than they are realistic, and heroes have far too easy a time using foreign systems.

titulo: Web 2.0 Can Be Dangerous...
descripcion: AJAX, rich Internet UIs, mashups, communities, and user-generated content often add more complexity than they're worth. They divert design resources and prove that what's hyped is rarely what's most profitable.

titulo: Intranet Information Architecture (IA) Methods
descripcion: In analyzing 56 intranets, we found many common top-level categories, labels, and navigation designs, but ultimately, the diversity was too great to recommend a single IA.

titulo: High-Cost Usability Sometimes Makes Sense
descripcion: Computing the net present value (NPV) lets you estimate the most profitable level of usability investment. For big projects, expensive usability can pay off.

titulo: Generic Commands
descripcion: Applications can give users access to a richer feature set by using the same few commands to achieve many related functions.

titulo: Passive Voice Is Redeemed For Web Headings
descripcion: Active voice is best for most Web content, but using passive voice can let you front-load important keywords in headings, blurbs, and lead sentences. This enhances scannability and thus SEO effectiveness.

descripcion: Measured usability improved by 44% compared to our last large-scale intranet study. The new research identified 5 times the previous number of intranet design guidelines.

titulo: Blah-Blah Text: Keep, Cut, or Kill?
descripcion: Introductory text on Web pages is usually too long, so users skip it. But short intros can increase usability by explaining the remaining content's purpose.

titulo: Feature Richness and User Engagement
descripcion: The more engaged users are, the more features an application can sustain. But most users have low commitment -- especially to websites, which must focus on simplicity, rather than features.

titulo: Multiple-User Simultaneous Testing (MUST)
descripcion: Testing 5-10 users at once lets you conduct large-scale usability testing and still meet your deadlines.

titulo: Defeated By a Dialog Box
descripcion: Interaction techniques that deviate from common GUI standards can create usability catastrophes that make applications impossible to use.

titulo: Change vs. Stability in Web Usability Guidelines
descripcion: A remarkable 80% of findings from the Web usability studies in the 1990s continue to hold today.

titulo: Should Designers and Developers Do Usability?
descripcion: Having a specialized usability person is best, but smaller design teams can still benefit when designers do their own user testing and other usability work.

titulo: Palm Foleo A Failed Mobile Device (Jakob Nielsen's Alertbox)
descripcion: Article about the limitations of the Palm Foleo "mobile companion" device, which was announced in May 2007 and cancelled in September 2007.

titulo: The Myth of the Genius Designer
descripcion: Having a good designer doesn't eliminate the need for a systematic usability process. Risk reduction and quality improvement both require user testing and other usability methods.

titulo: Location Is Irrelevant for Usability Studies
descripcion: You get the same insights regardless of where you conduct user testing, so there's no reason to test in multiple cities. When a city is dominated by your own industry, however, you should definitely test elsewhere.

titulo: Command Links
descripcion: Application commands can be presented as buttons or as links, which offer more room for explanation. For primary commands, however, buttons are still best.

titulo: Designing Effective Infographics
descripcion: Information graphics translate data into a visual medium that is easy to understand and engaging, aiming to integrate text and pictures.

titulo: UX Guidelines for Ecommerce Homepages, Category Pages, and Product Listing Pages
descripcion: Streamline users’ path to products by providing clear, differentiating product information at all levels — from the homepage to product listing pages.

titulo: Prominence-Interpretation Theory

descripcion: Prominence-interpretation theory helps determine what shapes users’ perceptions of a site’s credibility.

titulo: Is Poor Usability Killing E-Commerce?
descripcion: User success rates on e-commerce sites are only 56%, and most sites comply with only a third of documented usability guidelines. Given this, improving a site's usability can substantially increase both sales and a site's odds of survival.

titulo: Reset and Cancel Buttons
descripcion: Most Web forms would have improved usability if the Reset button was removed. Cancel buttons are also often of little value on the Web.

titulo: SEO and Usability
descripcion: What makes a website good will also give it a high SERP rank, but overly tricky search engine optimization can undermine the user experience.

titulo: Adding an Item to a Shopping Cart: Provide Clear, Persistent Feedback
descripcion: To confirm that an item has been added to cart, show a number badge and a confirmation popover or page, and change the label of the Add to Cart button, while preserving the ability to add multiples of that item.

titulo: The State of Transactional Email
descripcion: Automated email messages are more usable than they used to be. Good transactional email should be concise, clear, and easy for users to process.

titulo: The State of Ecommerce Search
descripcion: Ecommerce search tools are easy to find, more efficient than in the past, and rely on autosuggestions and facets to guide users through the search space.

titulo: Distracted Driving: UX’s Responsibility to Do No Harm
descripcion: I walked away from two distracted-driving accidents in one week. Can we use known UX principles to reduce harm?

titulo: Kindle 2 Usability Review
descripcion: Amazon's new e-book reader offers print-level readability and shines for reading fiction, but it has awkward interaction design and poor support for non-linear content.

titulo: Write for Reuse
descripcion: Users often see online content out of context and read it with different goals than you envisioned. While you can't predict all such goals, you can plan for multiple uses of your text.

titulo: Mobile Web 2009 = Desktop Web 1998
descripcion: Mobile phone users struggle mightily to use websites, even on high-end devices. To solve the problems, websites should provide special mobile versions.

titulo: Macintosh: 25 Years
descripcion: Although its individual features weren't new, the Mac offered integration, the expectation of a GUI, and interface consistency. Is the iPhone the Mac of mobile?

titulo: Press Area Usability
descripcion: As 3 studies of journalists show, they use the Web as a major research tool, exhibit high search dominance, and are impatient with bloated sites that don't serve their needs or list a PR contact.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
descripcion: 3 design guidelines for sending press releases to journalists by email.

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
descripcion: 22 case studies of failed PR information on corporate websites, with examples of when journalists decided to leave a site during story research.

titulo: Interaction Elasticity
descripcion: Usage goes down as interaction costs increase. User motivation determines how fast demand drops, following an elasticity curve.

titulo: Agile Development Projects and Usability
descripcion: Agile methods aim to overcome usability barriers in traditional development, but pose new threats to user experience quality. By modifying Agile approaches, however, many companies have realized the benefits without the pain.

titulo: Aspects of Design Quality
descripcion: Usability scores for 51 websites show some correlation between navigation, content, and feature quality, but no connections to other usability areas.

titulo: 10 Best Application UIs
descripcion: Many winners employ dashboards to give users a single overview of complex information and use lightboxes to ensure that users notice dialogs. Also, the Office 2007 ribbon showed surprisingly strong early adoption.

titulo: Reduce Bounce Rates: Fight for the Second Click
descripcion: Different traffic sources imply different reasons for why visitors might immediately leave your site. Design to keep deep-link followers engaged through additional pageviews.

titulo: Extreme Usability: How to Make an Already-Great Design Even Better
descripcion: The 1% of websites that don't suck can be made even better by strengthening exceptional user performance, eliminating miscues, and targeting company-wide use and unmet needs.

titulo: Link List Color on Intranets
descripcion: Lists of links are an intermediate case between content-embedded links and menu items. Showing listed links in blue or in the site's main link color is the recommended design - and the one most intranets follow.

titulo: 25 Years in Usability
descripcion: Since I started in 1983, the usability field has grown by 5,000%. It's a wonderful job - and still a promising career choice for new people.

titulo: Right-Justified Navigation Menus Impede Scannability
descripcion: Users scan lists by moving their eyes rapidly down the left edge. Menu items that are right-aligned make scanning more difficult.

titulo: Company Name First in Microcontent? Sometimes!
descripcion: Typically, you should deemphasize your company's name in links, but a new guideline recommends frontloading the name for search engine links under certain conditions.

titulo: Bridging the Designer-User Gap
descripcion: Depending on how representative designers are of the target audience, a project might need more or less user testing. Still, usability concerns never go away completely.

titulo: Four Bad Designs
descripcion: Bad content, bad links, bad navigation, bad category pages... which is worst for business? In these examples, bad content takes the prize for costing the company the most money.

titulo: 6 Tips for Successful Personalization
descripcion: Well-designed personalization carefully considers the creation of roles or types, ensures content is available for roles, and retains user control over the experience.

titulo: 7 Tips for Successful Customization
descripcion: Customization tools must be simple-to-use, easy-to-find, and easily edited, with both a clear intent and a clear benefit to users.

titulo: Customization vs. Personalization in the User Experience
descripcion: Customization gives control to the user and personalization gives control to the site. Both can enhance experiences, but only when carefully implemented.

titulo: Intranet Portals: Personalization Hot, Mobile Weak | Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: 19 new case studies of enterprise portals find slow growth in new features; the focus is on robust integration and formalizing governance.

titulo: Personalization is Over-Rated
descripcion: Personalized Web interfaces are over-hyped: users don't want to be stereotyped and it is too much work for them to enter detailed preference settings.

titulo: Transactional Email and Confirmation Messages
descripcion: Automated email can improve customer service, strengthen relationships, and help websites bypass search engines. But most messages fared poorly in user testing and didn't fulfill this potential.

titulo: Anybody Can Do Usability
descripcion: Usability is like cooking: everybody needs the results, anybody can do it reasonably well with a bit of training, and yet it takes a master to produce a gourmet outcome.

titulo: Velocity of Media Consumption: TV vs. the Web
descripcion: The granularity of user decisions is much finer on the Web, which is dominated by the instant gratification of the user's needs in any given instant. Content must cater to this rapid pace.

titulo: Writing for Social Media: Usability of Corporate Content
etiquetas: Content Strategy,Social Media,Writing for the Web
descripcion: Usability studies of corporate content distributed through Twitter, Facebook, MySpace, and LinkedIn: users like the simplicity of messages that pass into oblivion over time, but were frequently frustrated by unscannable writing, overly frequent postings, and their inability to locate companies on social networks.

titulo: Fresh vs. Familiar: How Aggressively to Redesign

titulo: Customization of UIs and Products
descripcion: Websites that let users customize the UI have the same measured usability as regular sites. Sites for customizing products, however, score substantially worse due to complex workflow.

titulo: Social Networking on Intranets
descripcion: Community features are spreading from 'Web 2.0' to 'Enterprise 2.0.' Research across 14 companies found that many are making productive use of social intranet features.

titulo: Mobile Usability, First Findings
descripcion: In user testing, website use on mobile devices got very low scores, especially when users accessed 'full' sites that weren't designed for mobile.

titulo: Building Respect for Usability Expertise
descripcion: Enemies of usability claim that because 'the experts disagree,' they can safely ignore user advocates' expertise and run with whatever design they personally prefer.

titulo: Guesses vs. Data as Basis for Design Recommendations
descripcion: Even the tiniest amount of empirical facts (say, observing 2 users) vastly improves the probability of making correct UI design decisions.

titulo: Investor Relations (IR) on Corporate Websites
descripcion: Individual investors are intimidated by overly complex IR sites and need simple summaries of financial data. Both individual and professional investors want the company's own story and investment vision.

titulo: IA Task Failures Remain Costly
descripcion: Task success is up substantially compared with usability statistics from 2004. Bad information architecture causes most of the remaining user failures.

titulo: Donation Usability: Increasing Online Giving (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: User research finds significant deficiencies in non-profit organizations' website content, which often fails to provide the info people need to make donation decisions.

titulo: Kindle Content Design
descripcion: Writing for Kindle is like writing for print, the Web, and mobile devices combined; optimal usability means optimizing content for each platform's special characteristics.

titulo: Annoying Online Ads Cost Business
descripcion: Increased advertising caused a 2.8% drop in use of an Internet service. The full magnitude of the lost business was only clear after a full year.

titulo: Top 10 Design Mistakes in the Unsubscribe Experience
descripcion: Canceling email subscriptions should be a one-click process, with no additional hurdles for users.

titulo: iPad and Kindle Reading Speeds
