titulo: Layered Interaction Analysis of Direct Manipulation (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Direct manipulation analyzed according to a detailed layered interaction model, showing that it has quite different effects on the dialogue on the different levels. In particular, the "no errors" claim may be true at the syntax level but not at several of the levels above or below that level.

titulo: Usability Metrics and Methodologies: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Trip report from a one-day seminar on usability metrics and methodologies, sponsored by the British Computer Society's human-computer interaction specialist group in connection with its 1990 annual meeting in London.

titulo: The Web in 2001: Paying Customers
descripcion: Offering free services on websites is not a sustainable business model, nor is advertising, which doesn't work on the Web. Most Internet companies are now pursuing an enterprise strategy to make money, but they'll soon begin turning to individual customers for revenue as well.

titulo: Alertbox 5 Years Retrospective
descripcion: Since 1995, the readership of the Alertbox has grown by 4,800%. Most of the 105 old usability columns remain valid to this day since people change more slowly than the technology. But the Alertbox has encountered some setbacks as well.

titulo: Predictions for the Web in Year 2000
descripcion: Micropayments will start with value-added content; mobile access; advice and sales become unbundled and physical experience environments may launch.

titulo: Metcalfe's Law in Reverse
descripcion: Partitioning the Web into N unlinked or otherwise isolated parts will reduce its overall value by a factor of N. A proprietary AOL instant messaging system will be worth only 4% of the full potential, and 1/3 will be completely lost.

titulo: Predictions for the Web in 1999
descripcion: Mobile access becomes 3rd Killer App for the Internet, Web standards rebound, customer service is automated, e-commerce patents are issued, and the Web has its own Y2K problems

titulo: Internet World 2008: Two Possible Futures: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's 1998 predictions of sessions he might present ten years later, at the 2008 Internet World conference.

titulo: Micro-Containers: An Example of Strategic Web Thinking
descripcion: Treating the Web as a strategic industry driver will lead to a patent bonanza where companies sew up entire ways of doing business. Distribution networks are discussed as one example of such a change

titulo: The Web in 1998: Some Predictions
descripcion: The Web will become more international (but will overseas sites or American sites benefit?), sites will outsource services, content will adapt to usage patterns in real time.

titulo: Changes in Web Usability Since 1994
descripcion: Most findings about Web usability from 1994 continue to hold. Scrolling pages and imagemaps are less of a problem; users now demand comprehensive sites.

titulo: Kill the 53-Day Meme
descripcion: One frequently finds newspaper articles about the Internet or the World Wide Web stating that the number of servers on the WWW is doubling every 53 days. I don't believe in the 53-day estimate any more.

titulo: Features for the Next Generation of Web Browsers
descripcion: There is now a profusion of choices when it comes to web browsers, and market shares can change rapidly. The only certain trend on the Internet and WWW is that change happens so quickly that it is impossible to predict what will happen. Even so, the following changes ought to happen, so hopefully they will be the next trends.

titulo: Coping with Information Overload: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Survey of methods used in various research systems for reducing information overload.

titulo: Future of Hypertext 1998-2015 (As Predicted in 1995) | Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Excerpt from Jakob Nielsen's 1995 book, Multimedia and Hypertext: The Internet and Beyond, offers predictions for the short term (3 to 5 year) and medium term (5 to 10 year) and long term (10 to 20 year) future of hypertext and the internet.

titulo: Mobile Devices Will Soon Be Useful
descripcion: New mobile devices and services are more realistic and useful than last year's models, and will likely expand mobile device adoption. Design usability and simplicity are key, particularly for the automotive market where complexity can be dangerous.

titulo: PC Forum 2001 Conference Report
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report for the 2001 PC Forum conference in Scottsdale, Arizona.

titulo: World Economic Forum Trip Report
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report for the 2001 World Economic Forum.

titulo: New Devices Augur Decent Mobile User Experience
descripcion: The current generation of mobile Internet products and services has miserable usability (as shown at the DEMOmobile 2000 conference). New devices like Blackberry, Modo, and a prototype Microsoft telephone do better.

titulo: Ten Biggest Thinkers of the 20th Century: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's 1999 list of the ten most important thinkers of the 20th century.

titulo: When Bad Design Elements Become the Standard
descripcion: Anything done by more than 90% of big sites becomes a de-facto design standard that must be followed unless an alternative design achieves 100% increased usability.

titulo: Give Me Your Billions: Internet Stock Valuation (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Unique visitors are a poor measure of user loyalty. Also, future users are late adopters and not likely to all patronize current popular sites. So beware of over-valuing Internet stock.

titulo: Failure of Corporate Websites
descripcion: Most corporate sites are so bad that Web usability problems cost a large company millions of dollars per year. On average, users fail when they try to accomplish tasks on the Web.

titulo: TV Meets the Web
descripcion: Comparing the nature of the Web as a medium when accessed through television sets and when accessed through computers, concluding that the level of user engagement is a main differentiator

titulo: Annual Themes of the CHI Conferences: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report overview of the Computer Human Interaction (CHI) Conferences from 1983 to 1994.

titulo: CHI'94 Trip Report: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report for the 1994 Computer-Human Interaction conference (CHI '94).

titulo: UPA'93 Trip Report: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report for the 1993 Usability Professionals Association (UPA) Annual Meeting.

titulo: CHI'92 Trip Report: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report for the 1992 Computer-Human Interaction conference (CHI '92).

titulo: CHI'90 Trip Report: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's trip report from the 1990 Computer-Human Interaction (CHI '90) conference.

titulo: Iterative Design of Sun's Website and Home Page (Jakob Nielsen)
descripcion: Extensive usability testing was conducted to guide the 1995 Sun Microsystems' Web site design. This series of articles describes in detail the methods and findings of the design team.

titulo: Flash: 99% Bad
descripcion: Flash reduces usability by: making bad design more likely, breaking the Web's fundamental interaction style, and consuming resources better spent enhancing a site's core value.

titulo: Parallel Design and Testing by Jakob Nielsen and Jan Maurits Faber
descripcion: How parallel design (a usability engineering method where multiple designers independently of each other design suggested user interfaces) can improve usability in the finished product.

titulo: Electronic Books - A Bad Idea
descripcion: The book metaphor is too strong and leads designers astray, missing out on the computer's potential for dynamic and interactive text.

titulo: Search and You May Find
descripcion: Search is the primary interface to the Web for many users. Search should be global (not scoped to a subsite) and available from every page; booleans should be made intimidating since users usually use them wrong

titulo: The Fallacy of Atypical Web Examples
descripcion: Common conclusions about Yahoo, Wall St. Journal, Disney, The WELL, and Amazon.com are wrong: generalizing Web trends from popular examples featured in the press is dangerous; spectacular case studies are often outliers

titulo: Profit Maximization vs. User Loyalty
descripcion: Instead of maximizing the profits from an individual visit it is better to encourage loyal users and establish non-monetary differentiation and frequent-user programs.

titulo: Usability as Barrier to Entry
descripcion: Increased user impatience will make new websites fail unless they are twice as usable as existing sites. Revolutionary Internet services must explain why users should care in no more than two lines.

titulo: Reputation Managers are Happening
descripcion: Epinions and Google join eBay in maintaining independent ratings of the quality of products, websites, and auction sellers, leading to better customer service and helping users make informed buying decisions.

titulo: Fighting Linkrot
descripcion: 6% of the Web's links are broken, diminishing its usability. All old URLs should be kept working indefinitely - otherwise you throw away business.

titulo: International Web Usability
descripcion: The unprecedented international exposure afforded by the Web increases the designer's responsibility for ensuring international usability. Because of the myriad of issues in international usability, I recommend doing international usability testing with users from a few countries in different parts of the world. No guidelines yet published are sufficiently complete to guarantee perfect international usability, so an empirical reality check is always preferred.

titulo: Why Yahoo is Good (But May Get Worse)
descripcion: Yahoo has great usability and huge traffic because it embraces the characteristics of the Internet medium: minimalist design and many structured links. But Yahoo may not scale to keep up with the growth of the net.

titulo: WebTV Usability Review
descripcion: Analysis of the usability of WebTV, including user interface guidelines for designing cross-platform Web pages that are considerate of WebTV users

titulo: Marginalia of Web Design
descripcion: Some "minor" details of web design--such as font size, text color, and image cropping-- can have important consequences for Web usability.

titulo: Social Media Outsourcing Can Be Risky
descripcion: Hosting a company's content and services on 3rd-party social networking sites involves both tactical risks (lower usability) and strategic risks (less user loyalty).

titulo: Nielsen Norman Group: UX Research, Training, and Consulting
etiquetas: Content Strategy,Corporate Websites,Writing for the Web
descripcion: 21 design guidelines for presenting press releases and news listing on corporate websites. Based on usability studies with journalists.

titulo: Corporate Websites Get a 'D' in PR
etiquetas: B2B Websites,Corporate Websites,Writing for the Web
descripcion: Corporations spend millions on PR, and yet the press sections of their websites often fail to meet journalists' most basic information needs. In our recent usability study, journalists found answers to only 68% of their questions across a range of corporate sites.

titulo: Global Web: Driving the International Network Economy
descripcion: Global use of websites leads to international usability problems and coping with the levels of Internet maturity in different countries; many of which are gaining rapidly

titulo: Impact of Data Quality on the Web User Experience
descripcion: Errors in data records destroy the usability of a site and make it difficult to find info. Guidelines for preventing, correcting, and surviving errors.

titulo: Goal Composition: Extending Task Analysis: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: This essay describes a technique for extending a task analysis based on the principle of goal composition. Basically, goal composition starts by considering each primary goal that the user may have when using the system. A list of possible additional features is then generated by combining each of these goals with a set of general meta-goals that extend the primary goals.

titulo: Information Retrieval of Imperfectly Recognized Handwriting
descripcion: Paper by Jakob Nielsen, Victoria L. Phillips, and Susan T. Dumais about the accuracy and error rates in handwritten input with a pen machine.

titulo: Three Large HyperCard Stacks: A 1989 Review: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's analysis of three CD-ROMs from 1989; focus on usability, hypertext structure, navigational dimensions and transitions (with screenshots of The Manhole, Whole Earth Catalog, Time Table of History)

titulo: Usability Insights From Sun Microsystem's 1997 Web Design
descripcion: The 1997 redesign of the Sun Microsystems' Web site aimed to improve the visual appearance, ease of navigation, and performance of the Web site.

titulo: Foreword to Rosenfeld and Morville's Information Architecture (1st ed)
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's foreword to Rosenfeld and Morville's book on Web Information Architecture (an O'Reilly Nutshell book). Your users will get lost unless you follow their advice.

titulo: The Network is the User Experience: Microsoft's .NET Announcement
descripcion: Microsoft's .NET strategy is a brilliant counter-move that reduces the Justice Department's proposed penalty to a victory in the previous war. Integrating the user experience at the network level opens the door to new and exciting services while diminishing the importance of traditional isolated websites.

titulo: Finally Progress in Internet Client Design
descripcion: Napster, IE 5 for the Mac, and Yahoo FinanceVision introduce specialized Internet UIs beyond the standard page viewing that had been unchanged since Mosaic.

titulo: User-Supportive Internet Architecture
descripcion: The basic ideology of the Internet is bit transport; we need a utility-focused human-centered ideology for its fundamental architecture and protocols.

titulo: Stuck With Old Browsers for at Least 3 Years
descripcion: 4% of users upgraded to a new version each month in 1998. By 2008, upgrade speeds were only 2%/month. It takes 3 years for 3/4 of users to embrace a new version.

titulo: Bill Gates' Shopping List to Build the Internet Desktop
descripcion: The Mac interface and its clones must die and be replaced by an Internet Desktop based on explicit quality ratings, micropayments, non-linear authoring, and a scriptable Web.

titulo: Does Internet = Web ?
descripcion: Advanced functionality requires Internet-enabled client-server software with optimized user interfaces that cannot be delivered in a Web browser. Reserve the Web for hypertext and content features.

titulo: The Telephone is the Best Metaphor for the Web
descripcion: The telephone is a better metaphor than television for thinking about the Web and its potential: the Web is a 1-to-1, narrowcast, low bandwidth medium that is user-driven and where everybody can publish content.

titulo: The Web Backlash of 1996
The Internet Desktop
How Much Bandwidth is Enough? A Tbps!
descripcion: In the long term we will need about a million times more bandwidth than a T1, as shown by the following list of requirements for the perfect user interface.

titulo: Relationships on the Web
descripcion: What will be the key to web-site survival this year? My bet is the establishment of relationships between the site and its users.

titulo: Prioritize: Good Content Bubbles to the Top
descripcion: If everything is emphasized, then nothing stands out. Prioritized design helps users focus on the most promising choices first.

titulo: Tracking the Growth of a Site
descripcion: Website usage must be tracked to plan server capacity needs and future business models. Examples show use of regression statistics to predict future traffic patterns.

titulo: Tagline Blues: What's the Site About?
descripcion: A website's tagline must explain what the company does and what makes it unique among competitors. Two questions can help you assess your own tagline: Would it work just as well for competitors? Would any company ever claim the opposite?

titulo: Review of Esther Dyson's Book Release 2.0
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen reviews Esther Dyson's book Release 2.0: useless, yet ultra-strategic; a tool to envision the network economy and the Web's eventual effect on our lives.

titulo: Slate Magazine - An Early Review
descripcion: Slate fails due to its inability to adjust to the online medium: too long articles, too little hypertext, scrolling home page (though redesigns have improved later issues)

titulo: Voodoo Usability
descripcion: Focus groups and surveys study users' opinions - not actual behavior - so they are misleading for the design of interactive systems like websites. Automated usability measures are just as misleading.

titulo: The Mud-Throwing Theory of Usability
descripcion: Instead of rushing new websites to a premature launch that will scare away your best customers forever, it is better to run a few fast usability studies in the beginning of the project.

titulo: Web Pages Must Live Forever
descripcion: Keeping old content alive will more than double the value of a site and only cost a small investment in content gardening. Removed pages equal lost users.

titulo: Mobile Phones: Europe's Next Minitel?
descripcion: Europe's cellular phone system is far superior to that in the United States. However, telephones will not be the platform for the mobile Internet. Given this, Europe's advantage may in fact be an obstacle to real innovations, as France's experience with Minitel shows.

titulo: Request Marketing
descripcion: The Web must reverse the traditional direction of marketing, and although once a viable paradigm permission marketing is no longer sufficient. Instead of a company generating messages when it wants to reach its customers, with request marketing, the company sends only messages that users ask for. Request marketing is especially suited to the mobile Internet, where intrusive messages are ultra aggravating.

titulo: Regulatory Usability
descripcion: Regulatory agencies should not transfer their rules from the print world unchanged to Web content that is being read in a different manner. Instead, regulations should concern the usability of the actual information and whether users understand it.

titulo: Why Doc Searls Doesn't Sell Any Books
descripcion: Changing to a new fulfillment provider caused a website to lose all sales. Reason: lower usability. In the future, reputation managers and web wallets will even the playing field and remove Amazon's temporary advantage as the fulfillment provider of choice.

titulo: Eyetracking Study of Web Readers
descripcion: Poynter study confirms older Web content studies: plain headlines work best; users hunt for info, often ignore graphics, and interlace sites.

titulo: Beyond.com - usability review by Jakob Nielsen: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Beyond sells software online - some downloadable and some on hard media. Good search, good disclosure of S&H, less useful shopping guides.

titulo: Intranet Portals: The Corporate Information Infrastructure
descripcion: An intranet should have a single home page that integrates a directory hierarchy, search, and news. Most intranets are chaotic, under-funded, and lack design standards, causing huge losses in employee productivity.

titulo: Details in Study Methodology Can Give Misleading Results
descripcion: Details in measurement methodology make the results of a recent market research study irrelevant for predicting real user behavior on the Web.

titulo: 2D is Better Than 3D
descripcion: People are not frogs, making it difficult to navigate 3D computer spaces: stick to 2D for most navigation designs. Shun virtual reality gimmicks that distract from users' goals.

titulo: When to Open Web-Based Applications in a New Window
descripcion: Applets are divided into two categories: functionality applets that need to open in a new window and content applets that should stay on the browser page.

titulo: Do Websites Have Increasing Returns?
descripcion: How much better is it to be a *big* website? Large sites can use their own hyperlinks to drive even more traffic, but small sites generate more value through focused content and microtransactions

titulo: Telephone Usability: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: "Data phones" would be more widely adopted if they functioned more like a computer with voice communication, rather than a telephone with data memory.

titulo: Evolution of a Home Page Design: Article by Jakob Nielsen
descripcion: Screenshots and descriptions of 9 of the homepage versions created for the Sun Microsystems' 1995 Web site redesign effort, and tested with users to optimize the layout and content.

titulo: My Foreword to Mullet and Sano's Book on Visual Design
descripcion: Jakob Nielsen's foreword to Designing Visual Interfaces: Communication Oriented Techniques, by Darrell Sano and Kevin Mullet.
